text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended a quiet week with active May near its high, having traded in a tight range throughout the day. But while May rose $1.00 to $311.00 a tonne, August ended unchanged at $307.70. Traders said the market was now supported by buyers prepared to come in below $310.00 on May.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed unchanged as prices consolidated recent gains and many players opted out of the market to contemplate the next move, market sources said. The May contract closed flat at 11.00 cents/lb while the deferred months ended 0.01 lower to 0.04 higher. After rallying to a recent high of 11.06 cents/lb basis May, the market failed to follow its recent pattern and slipped back to the lower end of the trading range. Some analysts said this was a bullish signal, particularly ahead of May's expiry in three weeks. Support was pegged at 10.78 cents/lb basis May.

RUSSIA - Total sugar imports in February rose 24.3 per cent on January's level to 113,000 tonnes, the State Customs Committee said. This is up 24.3 per cent on January's level, it was added. Total white sugar imports from the Ukraine in February amounted to 65,800 tonnes while imports from Cuba reached 22,300 tonnes. Total imports in 1996 reached 3.236 million tonnes, raw value, compared with 3.186 million tonnes in 1995.

UKRAINE - Sugar exports in February 1997 reached 93,900 tonnes, white value, up from the January figure of 48,800 tonnes. The largest country of destination in February 1997 was Russia with 53,100 tonnes compared to 31,600 tonnes, Belarus with 6,300 tonnes compared to 1,600 tonnes and Azerbaijan with 4,900 tonnes against 2,500 tonnes.

PORTUGAL - Sugar imports in November 1996 reached 35,172 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 19,431 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first 11 months of 1996 (January/November) up to 279,185 tonnes compared to 286,664 tonnes in 1995 and 320,028 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/November 1996 were Swaziland with 57,013 tonnes raws against 35,362 tonnes, Mauritius with 42,962 tonnes, up from 18,119 tonnes, Zimbabwe with 33,747 tonnes compared to 36,169 tonnes and Jamaica with 31,756 tonnes compared to nil. Sugar exports in January/November 1996 reached 13,618 tonnes compared to 10,199 tonnes in 1995. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 15,432 tonnes against 7,434 tonnes in 1994. The major country of destination in January/November 1996 was Spain with 8,898 tonnes whites against 3,737 tonnes in 1995.

USA - Sugar imports under the 1996/97 (October/September) tariff rate quota up to March 31 amounted to 785,714 tonnes, raw value. This is equivalent to 41 per cent of the total quota of 1.9 million tonnes.

JAPAN- Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 64,240 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from 113,291 tonnes imported in January 1997 and 117,213 tonnes in February 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996/97 (October/February) up to 682,382 tonnes compared to 726,776 tonnes in the same year-ago period. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.681 million tonnes compared to 1.716 million tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in October/February 1996/97 were Australia with 370,809 tonnes raws against 394,343 tonnes, Thailand with 138,604 tonnes compared to 199,299 tonnes and South Africa with 114,542 tonnes against 129,768 tonnes.
